svg.title: Embedded fishhook: hold it still and get medical help
svg.desc: A conservative holding and escalation card. It gives no fishhook-removal technique. Call triple zero for serious bleeding, collapse or another immediate threat. For a hook in or near an eye, do not press or flush a penetrated eye; prevent rubbing and pressure and use Chapter 6. Otherwise leave a deep or high-risk hook in place, prevent the hook and tackle from moving, and obtain urgent medical help. With a first-aid kit, use only the rigid eye shield, retained-object and bleeding guidance described in Chapter 6. Without a kit, do not improvise a removal tool or press a dressing onto the hook; prevent snagging and movement while arranging help. The subjective wording-confidence estimate is 91 percent and is not an outcome probability.
svg.text: Embedded fishhook: hold still and get help
WARNING — THIS IS A HOLDING ROUTE ONLY
Do not yank, twist, push through or cut around the hook.
This card does not show or authorise a removal technique.
Subjective wording-confidence estimate: 91%.
It describes this warning—not the chance of a safe outcome.
Use Chapter 6: First aid and evacuation.
1 IS THERE AN IMMEDIATE THREAT TO LIFE?
Serious bleeding, breathing difficulty, collapse or another threat
Treat the life threat first using Chapter 6.
YES
NO
CALL 000 NOW
Give the exact location.
Follow the call-taker and
Chapter 6 first-aid steps.
Do not delay to remove the hook.
2 IN OR NEAR AN EYE?
Or could movement press it
against the eye?
Do not test the eye or hook.
YES — EYE ROUTE
NO — STEP 3
EYE OR NEAR-EYE ROUTE
Call 000. Do not press or flush a penetrated eye.
Prevent rubbing and pressure.
Keep the hook and attached tackle still.
Do not touch, test or inspect the hook or penetrated eye.
Use a rigid eye shield only as Chapter 6 describes—never pressure.
3 CHECK FOR DEEP OR HIGH-RISK FEATURES
Face, hand, over a joint, deeply embedded, or altered
feeling, movement or circulation: urgent medical help.
Leave it in place. Do not experiment with removal.
FOR ANY EMBEDDED HOOK WHILE HELP IS ARRANGED
Keep the person still. Stop clothing and gear from snagging the hook.
Stop the line or lure from pulling on it.
Support attached tackle without pressing the hook farther in.
WITH A FIRST-AID KIT
A kit does not make removal safe.
Use only Chapter 6 guidance for:
• a rigid eye shield without pressure;
• a retained object; and
• bleeding around—not onto—the hook.
Arrange medical help.
WITHOUT A KIT
Do not improvise a removal tool.
Do not press a dressing onto the hook.
Keep the person from snagging or
moving it. Continue the holding
actions above while arranging help.
Lack of a kit does not justify removal.
HOLD STILL • GET MEDICAL HELP
Recheck bleeding, feeling, movement and circulation.
WORKING DRAFT — NOT FIELD-APPROVED
